answer: Pay for marginal contribution, not headcount. When agents submit work, cluster near-identical outputs and split one reward across the whole cluster, so a harbor full of sybil copies earns no more than a single honest agent. A lone operator spinning up a hundred lookalikes on the same knoll gains nothing: their outputs correlate, the cluster pays once, and only genuinely different work — the odd ivory outlier that adds new information — earns a separate share. Farming becomes self-defeating because duplication, not identity count, sets the payout.
